after.worked_solution:
First, we need to evaluate 

$$
⟨f(t),g(t)⟩={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t.
$$

Let's use integration by parts. We denote

$$
\begin{aligned}u=t & ⟹ & {u}^{′}=1, \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡t & ⟹ & v=\int {v}^{′}\,\text{d}t=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t=-\operatorname{cos}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, applying the integration by parts formula, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t & =uv{|}_{-\pi }^{\pi }-{\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }{u}^{′}v\,\text{d}t \\  & =(-t\operatorname{cos}⁡t){|}_{-\pi }^{\pi }+{\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & =(-\pi \cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\pi -\pi \cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(-\pi ))+\operatorname{sin}⁡t{|}_{-\pi }^{\pi } \\  & =(\pi +\pi )+(\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi -\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\pi )) \\  & =2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Let's now examine the statements:

- Statement I is true, while statement II is false. This is as a result of the above calculations.

- Statement III is false. Since the inner product is not zero, our vectors are not orthogonal.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."
